sections.title: The spondyloarthritis family and its causes

blocks.text: The **spondyloarthropathies (SpA)** are a group of overlapping inflammatory diseases of the spine, peripheral joints and entheses that share a link with **HLA-B27**. Members: **axial SpA / ankylosing spondylitis (AS)**, **reactive arthritis (ReA)**, **psoriatic arthritis (PsA)** and **enteropathic (IBD-associated) arthritis**; when typical features occur without a recognised trigger the label is _undifferentiated SpA_. They are called **seronegative** because rheumatoid factor and ACPA are absent.

blocks.title: Features the whole family shares
items: Asymmetrical oligoarthritis, mainly of the **lower limbs**
**Inflammatory back pain** and **sacroiliitis**
**Enthesitis** (inflammation where tendon or ligament attaches to bone) and **dactylitis** (a whole "sausage" digit)
Extra-articular: **anterior uveitis**, psoriasis, sterile urethritis/prostatitis, IBD, aortic root disease (aortic regurgitation, conduction block)
Family clustering and **HLA-B27** carriage; RF negative

blocks.title: How the causes fit together
rows: Carried by >90% of people with AS versus about 8% of controls in Kumar (Davidson gives 9% of white Europeans). Only ~2% of carriers develop AS (about 20% if a first-degree relative is affected). Explains only ~30% of the genetic risk.
Concordance up to 70% in identical twins versus 20–25% in non-identical twins: strong but not purely genetic.
**ERAP-1** (processes peptides for HLA-B27), **IL-23 receptor**, **STAT3**. Misfolded HLA-B27 may trigger ER stress and cytokine release.
An abnormal immune response to gut bacteria in susceptible hosts; increased faecal _Klebsiella aerogenes_ reported in AS.
**IL-23 → IL-17** (Th17 cells) and **TNF-α** drive enthesitis and sacroiliitis; IL-22 promotes new bone formation. These are the drug targets.

blocks.title: Triggers and associated diseases
items: Enteric infection (reactive arthritis): _Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Campylobacter_
Sexually acquired infection (reactive arthritis): _Chlamydia trachomatis_, _Ureaplasma urealyticum_
Associated disease: psoriasis (psoriatic arthritis) and Crohn’s disease / ulcerative colitis (enteropathic arthritis)

blocks.note: Look at: the pathway from gut flora to dendritic cells, then IL-23 to IL-17-producing cells to sacroiliitis/enthesitis, with TNF-α alongside and IL-22 driving new bone.

blocks.text: **Enthesitis is the signature lesion** of SpA, whereas RA is centred on synovium. Typical sites: Achilles insertion, plantar fascia origin, patellar ligament, greater trochanter and humeral epicondyles. Widespread enthesal pain can be mislabelled as fibromyalgia.
**HLA-B27 is neither necessary nor sufficient.** It is common in healthy people, so a positive test only supports a diagnosis that already looks likely clinically.

sections.title: Axial SpA and ankylosing spondylitis: clinical picture

blocks.text: **Axial SpA** (about 1% of people) affects the sacroiliac joints and spine; early inflammation is visible on **MRI**. Once sacroiliitis shows on **plain X-ray** the disease is called **ankylosing spondylitis** (radiographic axSpA). Not every case of axSpA progresses to AS. AS typically starts in the **late teens or twenties**, with **male:female about 3:1** and a prevalence below 0.5%.

blocks.title: Inflammatory back pain (ASAS, Davidson)
items: Back pain for **more than 3 months** with at least **4 of 5**: better with exercise; not eased by rest; insidious onset; pain at night; onset **before age 45**
Morning stiffness in the low back and buttocks, easing with activity
Supportive: good response to NSAIDs, family history of SpA, history of IBD

blocks.title: Examination findings
items: Early: the lumbar lordosis is **retained** (the low back fails to flatten) on forward flexion; lumbar movement is limited in both the sagittal and frontal planes
**Reduced chest expansion** (under ~2.5 cm at the 4th intercostal space) from costovertebral involvement
Late "question-mark" posture: flattened lumbar spine, exaggerated thoracic kyphosis, compensatory neck hyperextension, fixed flexion at hips and knees; paraspinal wasting
Up to 40% have asymmetrical large-joint arthritis or enthesitis (plantar fasciitis, Achilles)

blocks.note: Look at: normal posture beside advanced AS posture: lost lordosis, thoracic kyphosis, neck hyperextension, flexed hips and knees.

blocks.title: Extra-articular features and complications of AS
rows: **Acute anterior uveitis**: the commonest extra-articular feature (~25%); may come before the back pain
Aortitis / aortic valve disease with **aortic regurgitation**; **heart block** from fibrosis of the conducting system
Restrictive defect from a rigid chest wall; rare **upper-lobe (apical) fibrosis**
Osteoporosis; a fused brittle spine can **fracture after minor trauma** and injure the cord

blocks.text: **Painful red eye with photophobia and blurred vision** in a patient with SpA means acute anterior uveitis, which is an **emergency** needing same-day ophthalmology.

The books give different frequencies. **Davidson** gives uveitis 25% and aortic valve disease 20%. **Kumar** gives uveitis ~30%, aortic incompetence in up to 1% and conduction defects in ~5%. Use Davidson’s figures; the stable exam fact is that **uveitis is the commonest extra-articular feature**.

Mouth ulcers do **not** fit AS: think of SLE or Crohn’s disease (or reactive arthritis). Most AS patients keep working with a normal life expectancy, especially if the spine fuses in an upright posture.

No single test makes the diagnosis. It rests on the **pattern of back pain + examination + imaging of the sacroiliac joints**, supported by **HLA-B27** and **CRP**. MRI finds sacroiliitis years before X-ray does.

blocks.title: Classification criteria
rows: **Sacroiliitis on MRI** + at least 1 SpA feature
Or **HLA-B27 positive** + more than 1 other SpA feature, even with no sacroiliitis on imaging
**Sacroiliitis on X-ray**: bilateral if mild, or unilateral if definite
Plus 1 clinical feature (inflammatory back pain, restricted lumbar movement, reduced chest expansion)

blocks.title: Tests and what they show
rows: **Bone marrow oedema** around the SI joints: the earliest sign, before X-ray change
Irregular, blurred margins with apparent widening, then sclerosis, narrowing and finally **fusion**
Vertebral **squaring** ("shiny corners"), fine symmetrical **marginal syndesmophytes**, ligament ossification and facet fusion giving the **bamboo spine**
Raised in active disease (ESR up in up to ~75%) but **can be normal**
Positive in ~90% of AS but in 6–8% of the population; most useful when suspicion is high and imaging is normal

blocks.title: Bedside measures and scores
items: **Schober’s test**: mark 5 cm below and 10 cm above the lumbosacral junction (dimples of Venus, ~L5). If the 15 cm gap grows by **less than 5 cm** (to under 20 cm) on full flexion, lumbar movement is restricted
**Chest expansion** and **occiput-to-wall distance** (the latter also rises in osteoporotic kyphosis)
Schober and occiput-to-wall are better for **monitoring** than for diagnosis
Activity and function scores: **BASDAI**, **BASFI**, **ASDAS-CRP**; the ASAS Health Index for overall health

blocks.note: Look at: coronal STIR MRI with bright bone marrow oedema on both sides of each sacroiliac joint and erosive irregularity (early axSpA).
Compare: fine, symmetrical marginal syndesmophytes (AS) with coarse, asymmetrical non-marginal ones (psoriatic spondylitis).
Look at: bamboo spine with symmetrical marginal syndesmophytes, fused sacroiliac joints and generalised osteopenia.

blocks.text: A **normal pelvic X-ray does not exclude axial SpA**: request MRI. Step-Up treats bilateral sacroiliitis as essential, but that applies only to established AS; non-radiographic axSpA has MRI changes only.
Age cut-off for inflammatory back pain: Davidson’s ASAS list uses onset **before 45**, while the Pocket Medicine "IPAIN" mnemonic uses before 40. Follow Davidson.

sections.title: Managing axial SpA and ankylosing spondylitis

blocks.title: Step-wise treatment
items: **Everyone**: education, daily exercise and physiotherapy (posture and extension work), stopping smoking
**First-line drug: an NSAID**, ideally once daily or slow-release at bedtime to cover night pain and morning stiffness. If one fails after 2–4 weeks at full dose, try another
**NSAIDs fail or are not tolerated → biologic**: a **TNF inhibitor** (adalimumab, etanercept, golimumab, certolizumab, infliximab) or the **IL-17A inhibitor secukinumab** (ixekizumab is another)
**Sulfasalazine / methotrexate**: only for **peripheral** arthritis; they do nothing for spinal disease or its progression

blocks.title: Specific problems
rows: Plantar fasciitis, enthesitis, a single peripheral joint

blocks.text: **Oral glucocorticoids do not help spinal AS.** Davidson reserves them for acute uveitis; some quick sources suggest steroids for flares, but follow Davidson.

IL-12/23 (ustekinumab) and IL-23 blockers work in PsA but **not in axial SpA** (Pocket Medicine). Kumar lists ustekinumab among alternative options in SpA, but Davidson gives only anti-TNF or anti-IL-17A for axial disease, so follow Davidson: for the spine choose anti-TNF or anti-IL-17A.

**Before anti-TNF**: chest X-ray for everyone, plus IGRA and specialist review in high-risk groups; treat active TB and give prophylaxis for latent TB first; assess hepatitis B and C; avoid in severe heart failure.
Neck or back pain after **even minor trauma** in AS means a possible fracture through the fused spine: immobilise until CT (± MRI) excludes it, to protect the cord.

blocks.note: Look at: a fused AS lumbar spine with a cleft through the fusion mass at L5–S1 after a car crash (a new fracture).

blocks.text: Anti-TNF eases symptoms but has **not been shown to stop ankylosis**, and disease relapses when it is stopped. **Early diagnosis** lets daily exercise start before syndesmophytes form; poor control leaves a fixed kyphosis that limits forward vision.

**Reactive arthritis** is a **sterile** synovitis that follows an infection elsewhere, usually within about **4 weeks**. It follows 1–2% of dysentery or sexually acquired non-specific urethritis episodes; **HLA-B27** raises the risk in men 30–50-fold. The sexually acquired form has a **male:female ratio of about 15:1**. Persisting bacterial antigen in the joint probably drives it.

blocks.title: Triggers
rows: Causes **septic** (gonococcal) arthritis rather than reactive arthritis

blocks.title: Clinical features
items: Young man with **acute asymmetrical lower-limb oligoarthritis** (knees, ankles, feet), which may move from joint to joint
Enthesitis (Achilles, plantar fascia), dactylitis, fever and weight loss
Classic triad (old name Reiter’s): **urethritis + conjunctivitis + arthritis**, "can’t see, can’t pee, can’t climb a tree"
Skin and mucosa: **circinate balanitis**, **keratoderma blennorrhagica** (pustular plaques on soles/palms), nail dystrophy, mouth ulcers
Anterior uveitis is rare in the first attack but occurs in ~30% with recurrent or chronic disease

blocks.note: Look at: the map of reactive arthritis features: conjunctivitis, mouth ulcers, urethritis, circinate balanitis, keratoderma on the sole, Achilles enthesitis, plantar fasciitis, sausage toe, knee effusion.

blocks.title: Investigations (a clinical diagnosis)
items: **Aspirate the joint**: fluid is sterile and neutrophil-rich; this excludes sepsis and crystals
ESR/CRP raised; RF, ACPA and ANA negative

Look for the trigger: first-void urine (mucoid threads on the "two-glass" test) and urine/genital NAAT for _Chlamydia_; stool culture (often negative by the time arthritis starts). Negative tests do not exclude ReA
Consider HIV testing
Chronic X-ray changes: periostitis, fluffy calcaneal spurs, enthesal erosions, **asymmetrical or unilateral sacroiliitis**, non-marginal syndesmophytes

blocks.title: Management
items: Rest, **NSAIDs** and analgesia; **intra-articular** steroid for a severe single joint, **systemic** steroid for polyarticular disease

Antibiotics only for an **identified** infection: chlamydial urethritis gets a short course of **doxycycline** or a single dose of **azithromycin**; uncomplicated enteric infection usually needs none. Screen and treat sexual partners
**DMARDs** (sulfasalazine or methotrexate) for persistent or recurrent arthritis or severe keratoderma; **anti-TNF** if DMARDs fail
Anterior uveitis is an emergency: topical, subconjunctival or systemic glucocorticoids

blocks.text: Course: most first attacks settle within months (6 months in Zero to Finals, up to 12 in Pocket Medicine), but 15–20% develop sacroiliitis and about 10% still have active disease 20 years later.
A hot swollen joint is **septic arthritis until proven otherwise**: aspirate for Gram stain, culture and crystals before calling it reactive.
Antibiotics do **not** change established reactive arthritis. Davidson finds no convincing evidence for them unless a triggering infection is found.

**Psoriatic arthritis** affects up to 40% of people with psoriasis in Davidson (quick sources give 10–30%). Davidson puts the usual onset at 25–40 years (Pocket Medicine gives equal sex incidence and a peak at 45–54 years; follow Davidson). It is strongly tied to **nail disease** (nail changes in ~85% of PsA). Arthritis comes **before the skin disease** in 13–17%, does not follow skin activity, and is associated with HIV.

blocks.title: Diagnosing PsA
items: **CASPAR**: inflammatory joint, spine or enthesis disease + **≥3 points** from: current psoriasis (2 points); psoriasis in a relative; psoriatic nail dystrophy; negative RF; current or past dactylitis; juxta-articular new bone on hand/foot X-ray
Bloods add little: ESR often normal; autoantibodies negative
X-ray: erosions with **new bone formation**, periostitis, **no periarticular osteoporosis**, **pencil-in-cup** deformity, ankylosis
Screen people with psoriasis using the **PEST** questionnaire

blocks.note: Look at: (A) a sausage digit (dactylitis); (B) DIP joint swelling with nail pitting and onycholysis.
Look at: forefoot X-ray with metatarsal head osteolysis and cupped phalangeal bases (pencil-in-cup).
Look at: arthritis mutilans hand with shortened, unstable (telescoping) fingers from osteolysis.

blocks.title: Treating PsA
items: Mild disease: NSAIDs/analgesia; **intra-articular steroid** for one inflamed joint; avoid splints and long rest
**Methotrexate is the first-choice DMARD** (also helps the skin); alternatives: sulfasalazine, leflunomide, ciclosporin; monitor LFTs

DMARD failure: **anti-TNF** (joints and skin), **secukinumab** (IL-17A), **ustekinumab** (IL-12/23 p40) or oral **apremilast** (PDE4 inhibitor; less effective; weight loss, low mood/suicidal ideation)
Manage jointly with dermatology

blocks.text: In PsA **avoid hydroxychloroquine** (can trigger severe psoriatic or exfoliative skin reactions) and **oral glucocorticoids** (can make the skin unstable when tapered). Single-joint steroid injections are fine.

blocks.title: Enteropathic (IBD-associated) arthritis
rows: Peripheral: large lower-limb joints, about 20% of IBD in Davidson (10–15% in Kumar and kcEssentials); Crohn’s > UC
**Tracks bowel activity**; remits with UC remission or colectomy but may persist in well-controlled Crohn’s; can come before the bowel symptoms
Axial: sacroiliitis/spondylitis (radiographic sacroiliitis in 20–25%), HLA-B27 linked

blocks.title: Treating enteropathic arthritis
items: Treat the IBD; intra-articular steroid for a single joint
**Sulfasalazine** is preferred to mesalazine because it helps bowel and joints; glucocorticoids and methotrexate also used
Biologics that treat both: **infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab, ustekinumab**

blocks.text: In IBD-associated arthritis, **avoid NSAIDs** (they can flare colitis) and **avoid etanercept** (it does not work for IBD). If symptoms worsen on anti-TNF, exclude bacterial overgrowth.

cards.front: Signature lesion shared by all spondyloarthropathies?
cards.back: **Enthesitis**: inflammation where tendon or ligament inserts into bone (RA is centred on synovium instead).

cards.front: HLA-B27 in AS vs the general population?
cards.back: >90% of AS patients vs about 8–9% of the population; only ~2% of carriers develop AS.

cards.front: Cytokine axis targeted by SpA biologics?

cards.back: **Acute anterior uveitis** (~25%); it can come before the back pain and is an emergency.
Aortitis with **aortic regurgitation** and **heart block** (conduction-system fibrosis).

cards.front: Earliest imaging sign of axial SpA?
cards.back: **Bone marrow oedema** around the SI joints on **STIR MRI**, before X-ray change.

cards.front: ASAS axSpA criteria in one line?
cards.back: MRI sacroiliitis + ≥1 SpA feature, **or** HLA-B27 + >1 SpA feature without sacroiliitis.
A 15 cm lumbar span (5 cm below to 10 cm above L5) grows by **<5 cm** on full flexion.
An **NSAID** (long-acting at night), plus exercise and physiotherapy.

cards.front: Next step when NSAIDs fail in AS?
cards.back: **TNF inhibitor** or **IL-17A inhibitor (secukinumab)**; sulfasalazine/methotrexate help only peripheral joints.

cards.front: Antibiotic for chlamydial urethritis in reactive arthritis?
cards.back: Short course of **doxycycline** or a single dose of **azithromycin**.

cards.front: Classic X-ray sign of psoriatic arthritis?
cards.back: **Pencil-in-cup** deformity with new bone formation and no periarticular osteoporosis.

cards.front: Which anti-TNF must be avoided in IBD-associated arthritis?
cards.back: **Etanercept**: it does not work for IBD.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has had 6 months of low back pain and bilateral Achilles heel pain. A rheumatology registrar explains that his condition, unlike rheumatoid arthritis, mainly affects the sites where tendons and ligaments attach to bone.
questions.leadIn: Which lesion is the hallmark of his disease group?
questions.explanation: Spondyloarthropathies are defined by **enthesitis**, inflammation at tendon/ligament insertions (Achilles, plantar fascia). RA is a synovitis.
whyNot: Pannus is the inflamed synovium of RA.
Tophi are urate deposits in gout.
Cysts and osteophytes describe osteoarthritis.
Nodules with vasculitis suggest RA or a primary vasculitis, not SpA.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old student asks for an HLA-B27 test because his father has ankylosing spondylitis. He has no symptoms. The test is positive.
questions.leadIn: Which statement about his result is most accurate?
options: Most HLA-B27 carriers never develop AS, though his affected father raises his risk
He will develop AS within 10 years
The result confirms he has non-radiographic axial SpA
HLA-B27 accounts for nearly all of the inherited risk of AS
A negative result would have excluded AS in future
questions.explanation: Only ~2% of HLA-B27 carriers develop AS; with an affected first-degree relative the figure rises to ~20%. HLA-B27 explains only ~30% of the genetic risk and is neither necessary nor sufficient.
whyNot: Most carriers never develop AS.
A gene test cannot diagnose a disease in someone without symptoms or imaging findings.
HLA-B27 explains only about 30% of the genetic risk.
Some patients with AS are HLA-B27 negative.

questions.theme: Extra-articular features and complications of ankylosing spondylitis
questions.leadIn: Match each patient with ankylosing spondylitis with the most likely feature or complication from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.

items.stem: A 28-year-old man with long-standing AS develops a painful red left eye, dislike of bright light and blurred vision over 1 day.
items.explanation: Painful red eye with photophobia is **acute anterior uveitis**, the commonest extra-articular feature of AS and an emergency.

items.stem: A 52-year-old man with fused-spine AS slips on a wet floor and lands on his back. He now has severe mid-back pain, although the fall seemed trivial.
items.explanation: A rigid, osteoporotic fused spine breaks with minor trauma: **fracture through a fused spine**; immobilise and image with CT.

items.stem: A 47-year-old man with AS has a collapsing pulse and a soft decrescendo murmur in early diastole, loudest along the left sternal border.
items.explanation: Aortitis in AS can lead to **aortic regurgitation** (early diastolic murmur, wide pulse pressure).

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman has 8 months of inflammatory-type low back pain with buttock stiffness. CRP is mildly raised and HLA-B27 is positive. Pelvic X-ray is normal.
questions.leadIn: What is the best next investigation?
options: MRI of the sacroiliac joints with STIR sequences
questions.explanation: X-rays lag years behind. **STIR MRI** shows bone marrow oedema of early sacroiliitis and can confirm axial SpA when the X-ray is normal.
whyNot: CT shows bony change but misses early inflammation.
Waiting delays diagnosis while MRI could show disease now.
A bone scan is non-specific and not the standard test.
These antibodies are negative in SpA and do not help.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has suspected AS. The examiner marks a point at the lumbosacral junction and another 10 cm above it, plus a third 5 cm below. On full forward flexion the marks 15 cm apart move to 17 cm apart.
questions.leadIn: How should this result be interpreted?
options: Restricted lumbar flexion supporting axial SpA
questions.explanation: In the Schober test an increase of **less than 5 cm** (here 2 cm) shows restricted lumbar flexion.
whyNot: A normal spine opens by at least 5 cm.
Chest expansion is measured with a tape round the chest.
Occiput-to-wall is measured standing against a wall.
Hypermobility would give a large increase, not a small one.

questions.leadIn: For each patient below choose the most appropriate next treatment from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.
options: Long-acting NSAID at night with daily exercise programme
Topical glucocorticoid with urgent ophthalmology review

items.stem: A 23-year-old man has just been diagnosed with axial SpA. He has night pain and 2 hours of morning stiffness. He has never had any treatment.
items.explanation: First line is an **NSAID**, ideally long-acting at bedtime, plus exercise and physiotherapy.

items.stem: A 31-year-old man with AS still has high BASDAI scores after two different NSAIDs, each taken at full dose for 4 weeks. He has had two attacks of acute anterior uveitis this year. Screening for TB and hepatitis is negative.
items.explanation: NSAID failure in axial disease → biologic. Anti-TNF and anti-IL-17A both treat the spine, but with **recurrent uveitis** a monoclonal **TNF inhibitor (adalimumab or infliximab)** is preferred. Conventional DMARDs do not help the spine.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman with AS is well controlled on an NSAID but has persistent plantar heel pain at the fascia origin.
items.explanation: Localised enthesitis such as plantar fasciitis responds to a **local glucocorticoid injection**.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man develops a painful swollen right knee and left ankle 3 weeks after a bout of bloody diarrhoea on holiday. He also has sore red eyes. Knee aspirate is turbid with many neutrophils; Gram stain and culture are negative and no crystals are seen.
questions.leadIn: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Asymmetric lower-limb arthritis and conjunctivitis within weeks of dysentery, with **sterile** neutrophil-rich fluid, is **reactive arthritis**.
whyNot: Culture and Gram stain are negative and two joints are involved.
No crystals were seen.
RA is a symmetrical small-joint polyarthritis without a preceding infection.
There is no known IBD; a single dysenteric illness points to a reactive trigger.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man has acute knee arthritis, dysuria and a painless rash on the glans penis. First-void urine NAAT is positive for _Chlamydia trachomatis_.
questions.leadIn: Which treatment should be added to an NSAID?
options: A short course of doxycycline (or single-dose azithromycin)
No antimicrobial at all because the joint is sterile
questions.explanation: Antibiotics do not change the arthritis, but an **identified** chlamydial urethritis must be treated (doxycycline or azithromycin) and partners screened.
whyNot: DMARDs are for persistent or recurrent disease, not a first attack.
The NAAT shows Chlamydia, not gonorrhoea.
Anti-TNF is kept for DMARD-resistant disease.
The infection itself still needs treating even though the joint is sterile.

questions.leadIn: For each patient below, pick the most likely diagnosis from the options above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.

items.stem: A 48-year-old woman with scalp psoriasis has swollen DIP joints of several fingers, with pitting and lifting of the nails. RF is negative.
items.explanation: DIP arthritis with nail pitting and onycholysis is the classic **psoriatic arthritis** pattern.

items.stem: A 33-year-old man with Crohn’s disease has a swollen right knee and ankle during a bout of diarrhoea and abdominal pain; joint aspirate is sterile.
items.explanation: Large-joint lower-limb arthritis that **flares with bowel activity** is peripheral **enteropathic arthritis**.

items.stem: A 41-year-old man has a swollen, painful whole second toe and Achilles pain. He has no rash, but his mother has psoriasis and his nails show pitting.
items.explanation: Two-step: dactylitis + nail dystrophy + family history score on CASPAR, so this is **PsA** even without skin disease (arthritis can precede psoriasis).

questions.theme: Causes of inflammatory joint and back pain in young adults
questions.leadIn: For each patient below, pick the most likely diagnosis from the options above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man has 9 months of low back and buttock pain that wakes him at night and improves after a hot shower and exercise. Pelvic X-ray shows bilateral sacroiliac erosions and sclerosis.
items.explanation: Inflammatory back pain + **radiographic** sacroiliitis = **ankylosing spondylitis**.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman has 7 months of inflammatory back pain and good NSAID response. Pelvic X-ray is normal but MRI shows sacroiliac bone marrow oedema.
items.explanation: MRI sacroiliitis with a normal X-ray = **non-radiographic axial SpA**.

items.stem: A 24-year-old man has a painful swollen knee, red eyes, dysuria and scaly pustular plaques on his soles, 2 weeks after unprotected sex.
items.explanation: Arthritis + conjunctivitis + urethritis + keratoderma blennorrhagica after sex = **reactive arthritis**.

items.stem: A 46-year-old man with psoriasis for 20 years has progressively shortened, unstable fingers whose skin folds concertina when the digits are pushed in.
items.explanation: Telescoping digits from osteolysis = **arthritis mutilans**, the destructive pattern of **psoriatic arthritis** (~5%).

questions.stem: A researcher studying ankylosing spondylitis looks for the cytokine pathway activated by gut-derived signals in dendritic cells that drives enthesitis and new bone formation.
questions.leadIn: Which cytokine pathway is central?
questions.explanation: Gut flora signals trigger IL-23 from dendritic cells, which drives **IL-17** from T cells and other cells; TNF-α also contributes and IL-22 drives new bone. This is why anti-IL-17 and anti-TNF drugs work.
whyNot: IL-4/IL-13 are Th2 (allergy) cytokines.
IL-5 drives eosinophils in asthma and allergy.
Interferon-alpha is linked with SLE.
IL-1 is central to autoinflammatory diseases and gout, not SpA.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with psoriatic arthritis has active arthritis in several joints despite NSAIDs. His GP suggests a DMARD.
questions.leadIn: Which DMARD should be avoided?
questions.explanation: **Hydroxychloroquine** can trigger severe or exfoliative psoriatic skin reactions. Methotrexate is first choice.
whyNot: Methotrexate is the first-choice DMARD and helps the skin too.
Sulfasalazine is an accepted alternative.
Leflunomide is an accepted alternative.
Ciclosporin is an accepted alternative and helps psoriasis.

questions.leadIn: For each patient below choose the single most useful next investigation from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.
options: MRI of the sacroiliac joints (STIR sequence)
Joint aspiration for Gram stain, culture and crystals
First-void urine nucleic acid test for Chlamydia
Chest X-ray and interferon-gamma release assay
Plain X-ray of the hands and feet

items.stem: A 30-year-old man has an acutely hot, swollen knee and a temperature of 38.4°C a week after diarrhoea. He is otherwise well.
items.explanation: A hot joint is septic until proven otherwise: **aspirate** for Gram stain, culture and crystals before diagnosing reactive arthritis.

items.stem: A 34-year-old man with AS is about to start adalimumab. He was born in a country with a high TB rate.
items.explanation: Before anti-TNF: **chest X-ray and IGRA**, with treatment of latent TB first.

items.stem: A 29-year-old man with axial SpA has new loose stools, weight loss and abdominal pain; stool cultures are negative.
items.explanation: **Faecal calprotectin** screens for IBD, which is common in axial SpA.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man has had low back pain for 1 year. It is worst at 4 am and on waking, when he is stiff for 90 minutes, and it improves when he goes to the gym. He had a painful red eye last year. Chest expansion is 2 cm.
questions.leadIn: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Step 1: the pain is **inflammatory** (over 3 months, night pain, morning stiffness, better with exercise, onset before 45). Step 2: past **anterior uveitis** is the commonest extra-articular feature of SpA. Step 3: **reduced chest expansion** shows costovertebral involvement. Together: axial SpA/AS; confirm with SI imaging.
whyNot: Mechanical pain gets worse with activity and better with rest.
Disc prolapse is acute, with radicular leg pain, not long morning stiffness.
Fibromyalgia does not cause uveitis or reduced chest expansion.
A fracture would be unusual at 27 without trauma or risk factors.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with ulcerative colitis has a painful, swollen left knee whenever her colitis flares. She also has 2 years of inflammatory back pain and MRI sacroiliitis. She has needed steroids three times this year for colitis.
questions.leadIn: Which biologic would best treat both her bowel and joint disease?
questions.explanation: Step 1: knee arthritis that flares with colitis = peripheral enteropathic arthritis; the back pain and sacroiliitis = axial disease. Step 2: she needs a drug that treats IBD **and** axial SpA. Step 3: monoclonal anti-TNF (**infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab**) does both; **etanercept** does not work for IBD.
whyNot: Etanercept has no efficacy in IBD.
Apremilast is an oral PDE4 inhibitor used in psoriatic arthritis; it is not a treatment for IBD.
Hydroxychloroquine is not a treatment for IBD or SpA.
Ustekinumab treats IBD but IL-12/23 blockade does not work for axial SpA.

questions.theme: X-ray and MRI appearances in spondyloarthritis
questions.leadIn: Match each patient with the imaging finding you would most expect, from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.
options: Bamboo spine with fused sacroiliac joints
Bone marrow oedema around the sacroiliac joints on STIR MRI

items.stem: A 58-year-old man has had AS for 30 years and now has a rigid spine with no movement in any plane. His sacroiliac joints are no longer visible.
items.explanation: Long-standing AS: syndesmophytes at every level, ossified ligaments, fused facets and SI joints, giving the **bamboo spine**.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman with psoriasis and nail pitting has deformed toes; the metatarsal heads look whittled away and the phalangeal bases are cupped.
items.explanation: Osteolysis of a whittled head sitting in a cupped base = **pencil-in-cup** deformity of PsA.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man has 6 months of inflammatory back pain. Plain films are normal; another scan shows bright signal in the bone next to both SI joints.
items.explanation: Step 1: normal plain films do not exclude axSpA. Step 2: STIR MRI shows **bone marrow oedema**, the earliest sign.

questions.leadIn: For each patient below choose the most appropriate next treatment from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.
options: Long-acting NSAID at night with daily exercise programme
Topical glucocorticoid with urgent ophthalmology review

items.stem: A 44-year-old man with plaque psoriasis has swollen MCP and DIP joints in both hands despite 3 months of NSAIDs. Liver function is normal and he drinks little alcohol.
items.explanation: First-choice DMARD in PsA is **methotrexate**, which also helps the skin.

items.stem: A 47-year-old man with long-standing AS, whose spinal symptoms are now controlled on adalimumab, has a DXA T-score of −2.9 and an old vertebral wedge fracture on his spine X-ray.
items.explanation: AS causes secondary **osteoporosis** with vertebral fractures; it is treated with a **bisphosphonate** alongside the usual AS care.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman with AS wakes with a painful red right eye, photophobia and blurred vision.
items.explanation: Acute anterior uveitis: **steroid eye drops** with same-day ophthalmology.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man with PsA has failed methotrexate and an anti-TNF. He has no history of depression and wants an oral drug.
items.explanation: Oral PDE4 inhibitor **apremilast** is an option after DMARD failure (less effective; watch weight loss and mood).

questions.theme: Imaging features that separate the spondyloarthropathies
questions.leadIn: Match each patient with the radiological finding most typical of their condition, from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.
options: Bamboo spine with fused sacroiliac joints
Bone marrow oedema around the sacroiliac joints on STIR MRI

items.stem: A 35-year-old man has AS confirmed by HLA-B27 and X-ray sacroiliitis. A lateral lumbar film shows thin vertical bony bridges joining the corners of adjacent vertebrae symmetrically.
items.explanation: AS produces **fine, symmetrical, marginal syndesmophytes**.

items.stem: A 49-year-old woman with psoriasis has back pain. Lateral spine X-ray shows bulky bony bridges on one side, arising away from the vertebral margins.
items.explanation: Psoriatic spondylitis gives **coarse, asymmetrical, non-marginal** syndesmophytes.

items.stem: A 32-year-old man has had recurrent reactive arthritis for 5 years with heel pain. A lateral foot X-ray shows ill-defined new bone at the plantar fascia insertion.
items.explanation: Chronic ReA: **fluffy calcaneal spurs** and periostitis at entheses.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man with chronic reactive arthritis has buttock pain. A pelvic X-ray shows erosions and sclerosis of only the left sacroiliac joint.
items.explanation: Unlike AS, sacroiliitis in ReA (and PsA) is often **asymmetrical or unilateral**.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man with AS has well-controlled back pain on an NSAID but develops a swollen right knee and left ankle (peripheral arthritis).
questions.leadIn: Which statement about sulfasalazine is correct?
options: It may help his peripheral arthritis but not his spinal disease
It is the drug of choice for axial symptoms
It is contraindicated in all spondyloarthritis
questions.explanation: Conventional DMARDs (sulfasalazine, methotrexate) help **peripheral** arthritis in SpA but have no effect on spinal symptoms or progression.
whyNot: No conventional DMARD has been shown to slow ankylosis.
Axial symptoms need NSAIDs, then anti-TNF or anti-IL-17.
It is used, especially in ReA and enteropathic arthritis.
Secukinumab blocks IL-17A; sulfasalazine does not.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man who has had AS for decades has slowly increasing breathlessness. Chest X-ray shows fibrotic changes in both upper zones.
questions.leadIn: What is the most likely cause of the X-ray change?
options: Apical pulmonary fibrosis associated with AS
questions.explanation: AS is associated with rare **upper-lobe (apical) fibrosis**, as well as restriction from the rigid chest wall.
whyNot: IPF is mainly basal and peripheral.
Methotrexate pneumonitis is diffuse, and methotrexate does not treat axial AS anyway.
LVF gives oedema and effusions, not fibrosis.
Asbestosis affects the lower zones and needs exposure.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman has a symmetrical polyarthritis of her hands. She has psoriatic nail dystrophy, her sister has psoriasis, and RF is negative. She has no rash now.
questions.leadIn: How many CASPAR points does she score, and does she meet the criteria?
questions.explanation: Inflammatory arthritis is the entry criterion. Points: family history of psoriasis (1) + nail dystrophy (1) + negative RF (1) = **3**, which meets CASPAR. Current psoriasis would have scored 2.
whyNot: She has three 1-point features, not two.
There is no dactylitis, X-ray new bone or current psoriasis to add a fourth point.
She has more than one feature.
She has no further features (current psoriasis, dactylitis or juxta-articular new bone) to raise the score to 5.

questions.leadIn: For each patient below, pick the most likely diagnosis from the options above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.

items.stem: A 36-year-old man who has ulcerative colitis develops a swollen left knee during a colitis flare. Earlier episodes settled each time the colitis went into remission.
items.explanation: Peripheral arthritis that tracks colitis activity = **enteropathic arthritis**.

items.stem: A 47-year-old woman has symmetrical small-joint hand arthritis, morning stiffness, positive anti-CCP and periarticular osteopenia with marginal erosions on X-ray.
items.explanation: Positive anti-CCP and periarticular osteopenia point to **rheumatoid arthritis**; SpA is seronegative.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman has widespread tender points at tendon insertions, poor sleep and fatigue. CRP is raised and she has had anterior uveitis. Pelvic X-ray is normal but MRI shows sacroiliitis.
items.explanation: Two-step: widespread enthesal pain is easily mislabelled as fibromyalgia, but raised CRP, uveitis and MRI sacroiliitis mean **axial SpA**; with a normal pelvic X-ray it is **non-radiographic** axial SpA.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man with AS has persistent axial disease despite two NSAIDs. He also has active plaque psoriasis. Latent TB screening is negative.
questions.leadIn: Which biologic is LEAST appropriate for his spinal disease?
questions.explanation: Davidson’s biologic options for axial disease are **anti-TNF** or **anti-IL-17A**, and both also treat the skin. IL-12/23 blockade (**ustekinumab**) helps psoriasis and PsA, but Pocket Medicine notes it **does not work in axial SpA** (Kumar lists it only as an alternative option), so it is the least appropriate choice for his spine.
whyNot: Secukinumab (IL-17A) works for AS and psoriasis.
Adalimumab works for the spine and the skin.
Certolizumab is a TNF inhibitor proven in AS.
Golimumab is a TNF inhibitor proven in AS.

questions.leadIn: Match each patient with ankylosing spondylitis with the most likely complication from the list above. Any option can be the answer for several patients, or for none.

items.stem: A 57-year-old man with long-standing AS develops urinary retention, saddle numbness and bilateral leg weakness over several months.
items.explanation: Slowly progressive sphincter and sacral nerve-root loss in AS = **cauda equina syndrome**.

items.stem: A 50-year-old man with AS has a slow pulse of 38/min and dizziness. ECG shows P waves unrelated to QRS complexes.
items.explanation: Fibrosis of the conducting system in AS can cause **complete heart block**.

items.stem: A 49-year-old man with AS has had a low-trauma wrist fracture. DXA shows a low T-score.
items.explanation: AS is associated with **osteoporosis** (treat with a bisphosphonate).

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man develops arthritis of his right knee 2 weeks after Salmonella gastroenteritis. The arthritis started after the diarrhoea had settled. Stool culture has now cleared.
questions.leadIn: Which statement about his management is correct?
options: NSAIDs are first line; antibiotics will not change the course of the arthritis
A 6-week course of ciprofloxacin will cure the arthritis
Methotrexate should be started at once
questions.explanation: Acute ReA is treated with rest, **NSAIDs** and joint injection if needed. There is no convincing evidence for antibiotics once the arthritis has developed, unless an infection is still present.
whyNot: Antibiotics do not alter established reactive arthritis.
DMARDs are kept for persistent or recurrent disease.
Systemic steroids are used for severe polyarticular ReA.
Anti-TNF is kept for DMARD-resistant disease.

ospe.identify: Coronal STIR MRI: high signal (bone marrow oedema) on both sides of the sacroiliac joints → **active sacroiliitis** of early axial SpA, before X-ray change.
**Bamboo spine** of advanced AS: symmetrical marginal syndesmophytes at every level, fused SI joints, osteopenia.
Syndesmophyte type: **fine, symmetrical, marginal → AS**; **coarse, asymmetrical, non-marginal → psoriatic (or reactive) spondylitis**.
**Dactylitis** (sausage digit) and **DIP arthritis with nail pitting/onycholysis** → psoriatic arthritis.
Forefoot X-ray: metatarsal head osteolysis and cupped phalangeal bases → **pencil-in-cup** deformity of psoriatic arthritis.
Shortened, telescoping fingers from bone resorption → **arthritis mutilans** (psoriatic arthritis, ~5%).
Features of **reactive arthritis**: conjunctivitis, urethritis, circinate balanitis, keratoderma blennorrhagica, enthesitis and sausage toe.
